core_dumped.description: Whether its process dumped core (ended by a signal).

duration_ms.description:
How long it ran, measured by the worker (the timestamps come from the master's wall
clock, so don't subtract them); none while it runs or for attempts ended by the master.

error_summary.description: The structured error summary (exception, message, traceback).

peak_memory_bytes.description:
The peak memory of its processes, sampled by the worker (about once a second); none
when it wasn't measured.

start_method.description:
How the worker started it: `spawn` (a new process: an interpreter for a Python task,
the command for a command task) or `fork` (from the fork server); none until the
worker reported its start.

status.description: How it ended (`success`, `failed`, `timed_out`, ...); none while it runs.

CommandView.description: A command: an action the master applies, then marks `applied` or `rejected`.

command_id.description: Its ID; poll `GET /api/v1/commands/{command_id}` for the decision.

result.description: What it produced when applied, e.g. `{"run_id": ...}` for a trigger.

dags.description: Every DAG not removed, in ID order.

conflict.description: Every place defining it, while it is in conflict (then it can't run).

oneOf.description:
Why it is held, while its file fails to import in its root's current code (decision
72): the scheduler creates no runs of it and manual triggers are refused until it
imports again. Not set for a timeout or a runner that died (the file is parsed again).
Where its current version is defined (none for a DAG only ever seen in conflict).

paused.description: Whether the scheduler is stopped for it.

trigger.description: Its trigger as in DAG JSON.

HeldView.description:
Why a DAG is held: its file's import error. The error is the **file's**, so every DAG of
the file is held (decision 72.3).

exception.description: The error's exception class name, e.g. `ModuleNotFoundError`.

path.description: The file, relative to its root.

reason.description:
What happened and what to do, for people: that the file failed (not only this DAG),
why, and how to fix it.

ImportErrorList.description: The import errors of each DAG root's current code.

ImportErrorView.description: A file of a DAG root's current code that failed to import (decision 66).

content_hash.description: The root's content hash that was parsed.

exception.description:
The exception's class name (`ParseTimeout`, `RunnerDied` or `ParseResultTooLarge` when
the worker stopped the file; `InvalidDag` when the master refused a DAG).

path.description: The file, relative to the root.
The file, relative to the root.

LogChunk.description: A part of an attempt's log, read from the worker that ran it.

content.description: The log's text (invalid UTF-8 replaced by `U+FFFD`).

next.description: The byte after `content`: where the next part starts.

running.description: Whether the attempt still runs (its log may grow).

size.description: The log's size when it was read.

worker_id.description: The worker it ran on (and that answered).

OutputView.description: A task's stored output in a run.

outcome.description: The outcome the task finished with.

value.description: The value it returned, as stored.

cancel_runs.description: Also cancel its queued and running runs.

code_hashes.description:
The code hashes its attempts ran with, in the order first used. More than one: its
tasks ran on different code (it changed during the run).

tasks.description: Its tasks, in task ID order.

runs.description:
Newest first: a DAG's by `planned_for`; the list over every DAG by `triggered_at`, then
run ID.

since.description: The start of its window, `(since, planned_for]`.

triggered_by.description: `scheduler`, a user name, the parent run, or `trigger`.

reason.description: Why it waits or can't be scheduled.

planned_for.description: The moment the run is for (`--for`); now if not given. Must not be in the future.

involuntary_context_switches.description: Times it was preempted; none as for `voluntary_context_switches`.

peak_rss_bytes.description:
The peak resident set size, in bytes; for a forked process it includes the pages it
shares with the fork server (`peak_memory_bytes`, the watchdog's PSS, doesn't); none
for a spawned process (its memory is gone when the worker reads it).

system_cpu_micros.description: CPU time in the kernel, in microseconds.

user_cpu_micros.description: CPU time in user mode, in microseconds.

voluntary_context_switches.description:
Times it gave up the CPU (waiting for I/O or a lock), with its threads and reaped
children; none for a spawned process (only its leader thread's could be read).

interpreter.description: The interpreter it concerns; empty if none.

workers.description: Every worker the master has seen, in ID order.

WorkerView.description: A worker in the registry (kept after it is gone, so its logs can be found).

drained.description: Drained for maintenance (`schedr workers drain`): no new tasks until resumed.

incarnation_id.description: The incarnation of its agent process it last registered with.

last_heartbeat_at.description: The last sign of life the master recorded (at most once per heartbeat interval).

log_endpoint.description: Where its log endpoint listens (where a gone worker's logs were served).

offline_at.description: When it went offline or was lost.

warnings.description: What is wrong with it now, as it last reported (e.g. a disabled fork server).

bearer.description: A token for a mesh or proxy in front of schedr that requires one; schedr itself checks none.

get.summary: A command and the master's decision about it.

post.summary:
Pause a DAG: the scheduler creates no runs of it (optionally cancelling those in
progress). Applied by the master; poll the command for the decision.

parameters.description: Only the runs for this moment (`--for`).
parameters.name: for

parameters.description: At most this many (default 50, at most 500).
parameters.name: limit

post.summary:
Start a manual run (`schedr runs trigger`). Applied by the master; poll the command for the
decision and the run's ID.
Unpause a DAG. Applied by the master; poll the command for the decision.

200.description: Server-sent events: `run` (`{"run_id", "dag_id"}`), `dag` (`{"dag_id"}`), `workers` (`{}`) and `refresh` (`{}`: anything may have changed)

get.summary:
What changed, as it happens: `run`, `dag`, `workers` and `refresh` events (see the module
documentation).

The files of each DAG root's current code that failed to import (decision 66). A DAG
defined in such a file keeps its last good version (still listed) but is held: no run is
created and manual triggers are refused until the file is fixed (decision 72). A timeout or
a runner that died holds nothing: the file is parsed again (72.2). Fixing the file and
syncing the root makes the entry go.

parameters.description: Only runs in this state: `queued`, `running`, `success`, `failed` or `cancelled`.
parameters.name: state

parameters.description:
Only runs triggered before this moment: the last listed run's `triggered_at`, for the
next page (with `before_run`).
parameters.name: before

parameters.description:
With `before`: the last listed run's ID, so runs triggered at that same moment (a
scheduler round triggers its runs together) are listed after it, by ID, not skipped.
parameters.name: before_run

parameters.description: At most this many (default 50, at most 500).
parameters.name: limit

get.summary:
Runs of every DAG, newest triggered first (then by ID); filtered by DAG and state, paged
with `before` and `before_run` (the last listed run's `triggered_at` and ID).

post.summary:
Cancel a run (`schedr runs cancel`). Applied by the master; poll the command for the
decision.

get.summary:
The commands about a run, oldest first: the trigger that made it, and cancelling it or
cancelling or retrying its tasks, with the master's decisions.

The DAG a run ran with: its version's DAG JSON (tasks, dependencies, settings), for its
graph.
The attempts of a run's task, oldest first.

parameters.description: The first byte wanted (0 by default): the `next` of the previous part, to follow a log.
parameters.name: from

parameters.description: At most this many bytes (1 MiB by default; between 4 bytes, one character, and that).
parameters.name: limit

get.summary:
A part of an attempt's log, read from the worker that ran it; read on from `next` to follow
a running task. 404 when the attempt has no log (yet), or the worker no longer has it; 503
when the worker is gone or can't be reached.

post.summary:
Cancel one task of a run (`schedr tasks cancel`): stopped if it runs, cancelled at once if
it hasn't started; the tasks downstream of it are cancelled. Applied by the master; poll
the command for the decision.

get.summary: A task's stored output in a run, with its outcome; 404 while it has none.

post.summary:
Retry an `unschedulable` task of an unfinished run (`schedr tasks retry`). Applied by the
master; poll the command for the decision.

get.summary: Every worker the master has seen, gone ones included.

post.summary:
Drain a worker for maintenance (`schedr workers drain`): no new tasks, its running ones
finish; kept across restarts until resumed. Applied by the master; poll the command for
the decision.

Let a drained worker take tasks again (`schedr workers resume`). Applied by the master;
poll the command for the decision.
